problems.problem: Let $p$ be a prime number. Find all natural numbers $n$ such that $p\mid\varphi(n)$ and for all $a$ with $\gcd(a,n)=1$ $$n\mid a^{\frac{\varphi(n)}{p}}-1.$$

Suppose $n$ coins are given whose masses are unknown. We have a balance, and each time we can choose an even number of coins and put half of them on one side of the balance and the other half on the other side, so that a comparison is made. Our aim is to determine whether or not the masses of all coins are equal. Show that at least $n-1$ comparisons are required.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle and $M$ the midpoint of $BC$. Suppose that $AM$ meets the incircle at $K$ and $L$. The lines through $K$ and $L$ parallel to $BC$ meet the incircle again at $X$ and $Y$. Suppose that $AX$ and $AY$ meet $BC$ at $P$ and $Q$. Prove that $BP=CQ$.
Let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ be real numbers. Prove that $$\sum_{i,j=1}^n |x_i+x_j|\geq n\sum_{i=1}^n |x_i|.$$

Let $ABC$ be a triangle whose circumradius is equal to the radius of its excircle opposite $A$. Suppose that this excircle touches $BC,AC,AB$ at $M,N,L$. Prove that the circumcenter $O$ of $ABC$ is the orthocenter of triangle $MNL$.

Let $G$ be a tournament whose edges are colored either red or blue. Prove that there exists a vertex $v$ of $G$ with the property that for every other vertex $u$ there is a monochromatic directed path from $v$ to $u$.

We have $n$ points in the plane, no three on a line. We call $k$ of them good if they form a convex polygon and there is no other of the points inside this convex polygon. For a fixed $k$, let $c_k$ be the number of good $k$-tuples of points. Show that the sum $$\sum_{i=3}^n (-1)^i c_i$$ does not depend on the configuration of the points but only on $n$.

Let $n$ be a fixed natural number.

(a) Find all solutions of the equation $$\sum_{k=1}^n \left\lfloor\frac x{2^k}\right\rfloor=x-1.$$ (b) Find the number of solutions of the equation $$\sum_{k=1}^n \left\lfloor\frac x{2^k}\right\rfloor=x-m,$$ where $m$ is a fixed natural number.

Let $l,m$ be two parallel lines in the plane and $P$ a fixed point between them. Let $E,F$ be variable points on $l,m$ such that the directed angle $EPF$ is fixed and equal to $\alpha$, where $0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}2$. Show that there is another point (different from $P$) from which the segment $EF$ is also seen under a fixed angle.

Let $n$ be a fixed natural number. Find all $n$-tuples of pairwise distinct and coprime natural numbers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ such that for $1\leq i\leq n$ $$a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n\mid a_1^i+a_2^i+\cdots+a_n^i.$$

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $D,E,F$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A,B,C$ to $BC,CA,AB$. Let $P,Q,R$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A,B,C$ to $EF,FD,DE$. Prove that $$2(PQ+QR+RP)\geq DE+EF+FD.$$

Suppose we have a simple polygon (that is, it does not intersect itself, but it is not necessarily convex). Show that this polygon has a diagonal which lies completely inside the polygon such that each of the two arcs into which it divides the boundary of the polygon (the two arcs have $2$ vertices in common) contains at least one third of the vertices of the polygon.
In a triangle $ABC$, $M$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $D$ is a point on $BC$ such that $DB=DM$. We know that $2BC^2-AC^2=AB\cdot AC$. Prove that $$BD\cdot DC=\frac{AC^2\cdot AB}{2(AB+AC)}.$$
Let $A$ be the largest subset of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ such that each $x\in A$ divides at most one other element of $A$. Prove that $$\frac{2n}3\leq |A|\leq \left\lceil \frac{3n}4\right\rceil.$$
Find all functions $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $$f(x^2+y+f(y))=2y+f(x)^2.$$

On a billiard table in the shape of an isosceles right triangle, a ball starts moving from one of the vertices adjacent to the hypotenuse. When it reaches a side, it is reflected. Prove that if the ball reaches a vertex, then it is not the vertex from which it started.
Find all monic polynomials $f(x)$ in $\mathbb Z[x]$ such that $f(\mathbb Z)$ is closed under multiplication.

Let $\omega$ be the incircle of a triangle $ABC$. Points $P$ and $Q$ on $AB$ and $AC$ are such that $PQ$ is parallel to $BC$ and tangent to $\omega$. The sides $AB,AC$ touch $\omega$ at $F,E$. Prove that if $M$ is the midpoint of $PQ$ and $T$ is the intersection point of $EF$ and $BC$, then $TM$ is tangent to $\omega$.

Does there exist a sequence $a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots$ of natural numbers such that $\gcd(a_i,a_j)=1$ for all $i\neq j$, and for each $n$ the polynomial $\sum_{i=0}^{n}a_ix^i$ is irreducible in $\mathbb Z[x]$?

Suppose $n$ lines in the plane are such that no two are parallel and no three are concurrent. For any two of the lines, their angle is a real number in $[0,\frac{\pi}2]$. Find the largest possible value of the sum of the $\binom n2$ angles between the lines.
$O$ is a point inside a triangle $ABC$ such that $OA=OB+OC$. Let $B',C'$ be the midpoints of the arcs $AOC$ and $AOB$. Prove that the circumcircles of $COC'$ and $BOB'$ are tangent to each other.
Find all polynomials $p$ of degree $3$ such that for all $x,y\geq 0$ $$p(x+y)\geq p(x)+p(y).$$

Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB=AC$. Through $A$ we draw a line $\ell$ parallel to $BC$. Points $P,Q$ on the perpendicular bisectors of $AB,AC$ are such that $PQ\perp BC$. $M,N$ are points on $\ell$ such that $\angle APM=\angle AQN=\frac\pi2$. Prove that $$\frac{1}{AM}+\frac1{AN}\leq\frac2{AB}.$$

Let $P$ be a point in a square whose sides are mirrors. A ray of light leaves $P$ with slope $\alpha$. We know that the ray never reaches a vertex. We form an infinite sequence of $0$s and $1$s: after each contact of the ray with a horizontal side we write $0$, and after each contact with a vertical side we write $1$. For each $n\geq 1$, let $B_n$ be the set of all blocks of length $n$ in this sequence.

(a) Prove that $B_n$ does not depend on the location of $P$.

(b) Prove that if $\frac{\alpha}{\pi}$ is irrational, then $|B_n|=n+1$.
Find all functions $f: \mathbb R\to \mathbb R$ such that for all $x,y\in\mathbb R$ $$f(xf(y)) + y + f(x) = f(x + f(y)) + yf(x).$$

Let $I$ be the incenter of a triangle $ABC$ and $l'$ a line tangent to the incircle. Let $l$ be another line which meets $AB,AC,BC$ at $C',B',A'$, respectively. From $A'$ we draw the tangent to the incircle other than $BC$; it meets $l'$ at $A_1$. The points $B_1,C_1$ are defined similarly. Prove that $AA_1,BB_1,CC_1$ are concurrent.
Suppose that $T$ is a tree with $k$ edges. Prove that the $k$-dimensional cube can be partitioned into graphs isomorphic to $T$.
Let $P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4$ be points on the unit sphere. Prove that $\sum_{i\neq j}\frac1{|P_i-P_j|}$ attains its minimum value if and only if these four points are the vertices of a regular tetrahedron.
Let $a,b,c > 0$ with $ab+bc+ca = 1$. Prove that $$\sqrt {a^3 + a} + \sqrt {b^3 + b} + \sqrt {c^3 + c}\geq2\sqrt {a + b + c}.$$

Prove that in a tournament with $799$ teams there exist $14$ teams which can be partitioned into two groups in such a way that each team of the first group has won against each team of the second group.

Let $S$ be a set with $n$ elements, and $F$ a family of $2^{n-1}$ subsets of $S$ such that $A\cap B\cap C$ is nonempty for all $A,B,C\in F$. Prove that the intersection of all elements of $F$ is nonempty.
Find all polynomials $p$ in one variable with integer coefficients such that whenever $a$ and $b$ are natural numbers with $a + b$ a perfect square, $p(a) + p(b)$ is also a perfect square.

$I_a$ is the excenter of triangle $ABC$ opposite $A$, and $AI_a$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $T$. Let $X$ be a point on $TI_a$ such that $XI_a^2=XA\cdot XT$. The perpendicular from $X$ to $BC$ meets $BC$ at $A'$. Define $B'$ and $C'$ in the same way. Prove that $AA'$, $BB'$ and $CC'$ are concurrent.

In a triangle $ABC$, $\angle B$ is greater than $\angle C$. $T$ is the midpoint of the arc $BAC$ of the circumcircle of $ABC$ and $I$ is the incenter of $ABC$. $E$ is a point such that $\angle AEI=90^\circ$ and $AE\parallel BC$. $TE$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ for the second time at $P$. If $\angle B=\angle IPB$, find the angle $\angle A$.
Let $k$ be a given natural number. Find all functions $f: \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for all $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ $$f(m)+f(n)\mid (m+n)^k.$$

In an acute triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the foot of the altitude from $A$ and $I_a$ is the excenter opposite $A$. $K$ is a point on the extension of $AB$ beyond $B$ for which $\angle AKI_a=90^\circ+\frac 34\angle C$. $I_aK$ meets the extension of $AD$ at $L$. Prove that $DI_a$ bisects the angle $\angle AI_aB$ if and only if $AL=2R$, where $R$ is the circumradius of $ABC$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle and let $A'$, $B'$, $C'$ lie on $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively, such that the incenters of $A'B'C'$ and $ABC$ coincide and the inradius of $A'B'C'$ is half of the inradius of $ABC$. Prove that $ABC$ is equilateral.
Let $a$ be a fixed natural number. Prove that the set of prime divisors of the numbers $2^{2^n} + a$, $n = 1,2,\ldots$, is infinite.
Let $a,b,c$ be positive real numbers such that $a+b+c=3$. Prove that $$\frac{1}{2+a^2+b^2}+\frac{1}{2+b^2+c^2}+\frac{1}{2+c^2+a^2} \leq \frac{3}{4}.$$
Find all polynomials $f$ with integer coefficients such that for every prime $p$ and natural numbers $u$ and $v$ with $p \mid uv - 1$ we always have $p \mid f(u)f(v) - 1$.

$ABC$ is a triangle and $AA'$, $BB'$, $CC'$ are its altitudes. Let $P$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $C'$ to $A'B'$, and let $Q$ be the point on $A'B'$ such that $QA = QB$. Prove that $$\angle PBQ = \angle PAQ = \angle PC'C.$$

We have a closed path on the vertices of an $n\times n$ square grid which passes through each vertex exactly once. Prove that there are two adjacent vertices such that if we cut the path at these points, then the length of each piece is not less than a quarter of the total length of the path.
Three directions in the plane are given. We draw $11$ lines in each direction. Find the maximum number of points of the plane which lie on three of the lines.
Find all polynomials $P(x,y)$ such that for all reals $x$ and $y$ $$P(x^2,y^2) =P\left(\frac {(x + y)^2}{2},\frac {(x - y)^2}{2}\right).$$

In a triangle $ABC$, $D$, $E$ and $F$ are the points where the incircle, with center $I$, touches $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$, respectively. Let $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to $EF$, and $P$ the midpoint of $DM$. If $H$ is the orthocenter of triangle $BIC$, prove that $PH$ bisects $EF$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB\ne AC$. $D$ is a point on the line $BC$ such that $BA = BD$ and $B$ lies between $C$ and $D$. Let $I_c$ be the center of the circle which touches $AB$ and the extensions of $AC$ and $BC$. $CI_c$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $T$. If $\angle TDI_c = \frac {\angle B + \angle C}{4}$, find $\angle A$.
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that $$3^{\frac{5^{2^n}-1}{2^{n+2}}} \equiv (-5)^{\frac{3^{2^n}-1}{2^{n+2}}} \pmod{2^{n+4}}.$$
$T$ is a subset of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ with the property that for all distinct $i,j \in T$, $2j$ is not divisible by $i$. Prove that $$|T| \leq \frac {4}{9}n + \log_2 n + 2.$$

Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be a non-decreasing function and let $n$ be an arbitrary natural number. Suppose that there are prime numbers $p_1,p_2,\dots,p_n$ and natural numbers $s_1,s_2,\dots,s_n$ such that for each $1\leq i\leq n$ the set $\{f(p_ir+s_i)\mid r=1,2,\dots\}$ is an infinite arithmetic progression. Prove that there is a natural number $a$ such that $$f(a+1),\ f(a+2),\ \dots,\ f(a+n)$$ form an arithmetic progression.
Find all non-decreasing functions $f:[0,+\infty)\to[0,+\infty)$ such that for all $x,y\geq 0$ $$f\left(\frac{x+f(x)}2+y\right)=2x-f(x)+f(f(y)).$$
Find all polynomials $p(x,y)$ in two variables such that for all $a,b,c\in\mathbb R$ $$p(ab,c^2+1)+p(bc,a^2+1)+p(ca,b^2+1)=0.$$

$S,T$ are two trees without vertices of degree $2$. To each edge a positive number, called the length of the edge, is associated. The distance between two vertices $v,w$ is defined as the sum of the lengths of the edges of the path between $v$ and $w$. Let $f$ be a bijection from the leaves of $S$ to the leaves of $T$ such that for any two leaves $u,v$ of $S$, the distance of $u,v$ in $S$ is equal to the distance of $f(u), f(v)$ in $T$. Prove that there is a bijection $g$ from the vertices of $S$ to the vertices of $T$ such that for any two vertices $u,v$ of $S$, the distance of $u,v$ in $S$ is equal to the distance of $g(u), g(v)$ in $T$.

Circles $W_1,W_2$ intersect at $P,K$. $XY$ is the common tangent of the two circles which is nearer to $P$, with $X$ on $W_1$ and $Y$ on $W_2$. $XP$ meets $W_2$ for the second time at $C$ and $YP$ meets $W_1$ again at $B$. Let $A$ be the intersection point of $BX$ and $CY$. Prove that if $Q$ is the second intersection point of the circumcircles of $ABC$ and $AXY$, then $$\angle QXA=\angle QKP.$$

Let $M$ be an arbitrary point on the side $BC$ of a triangle $ABC$. A circle $W$ is tangent to $AB$ and $BM$ at $T$ and $K$ and is tangent to the circumcircle of $AMC$ at $P$. Prove that if $TK\parallel AM$, then the circumcircles of $APT$ and $KPC$ are tangent to each other.

Without lifting the pen from the paper, we draw a polygon in such a way that of any two adjacent sides one is vertical. In addition, while drawing the polygon, all vertical sides are drawn from top to bottom. Prove that this polygon intersects itself.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle with $BC>AB=AC$. $D,M$ are the midpoints of $BC$ and $AB$, respectively. $X$ is a point such that $BX\perp AC$ and $XD\parallel AB$. $BX$ and $AD$ meet at $H$. If $P$ is the intersection point of $DX$ and the circumcircle of $AHX$ (other than $X$), prove that the tangent from $A$ to the circumcircle of triangle $AMP$ is parallel to $BC$.

A sequence of real numbers $a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{1389}$ is called concave if $a_i\geq\frac{a_{i-1}+a_{i+1}}2$ for each $0<i<1389$. Find the largest $c$ such that for every concave sequence of non-negative real numbers $$\sum_{i=0}^{1389}ia_i^2\geq c\sum_{i=0}^{1389}a_i^2.$$

In every $1\times1$ square of an $m\times n$ table one of the two diagonals is drawn. Prove that there is a path along these diagonals either from the left side to the right side, or from the upper side to the lower side.

Let $O$ and $H$ be the circumcenter and the orthocenter of a triangle $ABC$. $M,N$ are the midpoints of $BH$ and $CH$. $BB'$ is a diameter of the circumcircle. If $HONM$ is a cyclic quadrilateral, prove that $B'N=\frac12AC$.
Prove that for each natural number $m$ there is a natural number $N$ such that for each $b$ with $2\leq b\leq1389$ the sum of digits of $N$ in base $b$ is larger than $m$.

In an acute triangle $ABC$ the angle $B$ is greater than $C$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and $D$ and $E$ the feet of the altitudes from $C$ and $B$, respectively. $K$ and $L$ are the midpoints of $ME$ and $MD$, respectively. If $KL$ meets the line through $A$ parallel to $BC$ at $T$, prove that $TA=TM$.

Find all natural numbers $n$ greater than $2$ for which there exist $n$ natural numbers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$, not all equal, such that the sequence $a_1a_2,a_2a_3,\ldots,a_na_1$ forms an arithmetic progression with nonzero common difference.

There are $n$ points on a circle ($n>1$). Define an interval as an arc of the circle whose endpoints are among these points. Consider a family $F$ of intervals such that for every element $A$ of $F$ there is at most one other element $B$ of $F$ with $A \subseteq B$ (in this case we say that $A$ is a sub-interval of $B$). We call an interval maximal if it is not a sub-interval of any other interval. If $m$ is the number of maximal elements of $F$ and $a$ the number of non-maximal elements of $F$, prove that $n\geq m+\frac a2$.

A finite set $A$ of natural numbers is called good if it satisfies the following conditions:

(a) for any three distinct elements $a,b,c$ of $A$ we have $\gcd(a,b,c)=1$;

(b) for any two distinct $b,c\in A$ there exists $a\in A$, distinct from $b,c$, such that $bc$ is divisible by $a$.

Find all good sets.
Find all surjective functions $f: \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ such that for all $x,y\in \mathbb R$ $$f(x+f(x)+2f(y))=f(2x)+f(2y).$$

A circle $\omega$ with center $O$ is given. From an arbitrary point $T$ outside $\omega$ draw the tangents $TB$ and $TC$ to it. $K$ and $H$ are points on $TB$ and $TC$, respectively.

(a) $B'$ and $C'$ are the second intersection points of $OB$ and $OC$ with $\omega$, respectively. $K'$ and $H'$ are points on the angle bisectors of $\angle BCO$ and $\angle CBO$, respectively, such that $KK' \perp BC$ and $HH'\perp BC$. Prove that $K,H',B'$ are collinear if and only if $H,K',C'$ are collinear.

(b) Suppose there exist two circles inside triangle $TBC$ which are tangent to each other at $J$ and are both tangent to $\omega$, one of them tangent to $TB$ at $K$ and the other tangent to $TC$ at $H$. Prove that the quadrilaterals $BKJI$ and $CHJI$ are cyclic, where $I$ is the incenter of triangle $OBC$.

Find the locus of the points $P$ in an equilateral triangle $ABC$ for which the square root of the distance from $P$ to one of the sides is equal to the sum of the square roots of the distances from $P$ to the two other sides.

Let $p$ be a prime and $k$ a positive integer with $k \le p$. Suppose that $f(x)$ is a polynomial in $\mathbb Z[x]$ such that $p^k \mid f(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{Z}$.

(a) Prove that there exist polynomials $A_0(x),\ldots,A_k(x)$ in $\mathbb Z[x]$ such that $$f(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{k} (x^p-x)^ip^{k-i}A_i(x).$$ (b) Find a counterexample for each prime $p$ and each $k > p$.

We have $n$ points in the plane, not all collinear. We call a line $\ell$ good if the $n$ points can be divided into two sets $A,B$ such that the sum of the distances of the points of $A$ to $\ell$ is equal to the sum of the distances of the points of $B$ to $\ell$. Prove that there exist infinitely many points in the plane through each of which pass at least $n+1$ good lines.

Find the least value of $k$ such that for all $a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{R}$ the inequality $$\sqrt{(a^2+1)(b^2+1)(c^2+1)} +\sqrt{(b^2+1)(c^2+1)(d^2+1)} +\sqrt{(c^2+1)(d^2+1)(a^2+1)} +\sqrt{(d^2+1)(a^2+1)(b^2+1)}$$ $$\ge 2( ab+bc+cd+da+ac+bd)-k$$ holds.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle and $A',B',C'$ the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Let $P$ and $P'$ be points in the plane such that $PA=P'A'$, $PB=P'B'$, $PC=P'C'$. Prove that all such lines $PP'$ pass through a fixed point.
Suppose that $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a function for which the expression $af(a)+bf(b)+2ab$ is a perfect square for all $a,b \in \mathbb{N}$. Prove that $f(a)=a$ for all $a \in \mathbb{N}$.
Find all positive integers $n \geq 2$ such that for all integers $i,j$ with $0 \leq i,j\leq n$, the numbers $i+j$ and $\binom{n}{i}+ \binom{n}{j}$ have the same parity.

Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of an acute triangle $ABC$, $D$ the midpoint of the arc $BAC$ and $I$ the incenter of triangle $ABC$. Let $DI$ meet $BC$ at $E$ and $\omega$ for the second time at $F$. Let $P$ be a point on the line $AF$ such that $PE$ is parallel to $AI$. Prove that $PE$ is the bisector of the angle $BPC$.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $S$ be a set of points in the plane with the following conditions:

(i) there do not exist $n$ lines in the plane such that every element of $S$ lies on at least one of them;

(ii) for every $X \in S$ there exist $n$ lines in the plane such that every element of $S \setminus \{X\}$ lies on at least one of them.

Find the maximum of $|S|$.

Consider $m+1$ horizontal and $n+1$ vertical lines ($m,n\ge 4$) in the plane forming an $m\times n$ table. Consider a closed path along the segments of this table which does not intersect itself, passes through all $(m-1)(n-1)$ interior vertices (each vertex is an intersection point of two lines) and does not pass through any of the outer vertices. Let $A$ be the number of vertices at which the path goes straight on, $B$ the number of squares of the table of which exactly two opposite sides are used by the path, and $C$ the number of squares of the table none of whose sides is used by the path. Prove that $$A=B-C+m+n-1.$$

The pentagon $ABCDE$ is inscribed in a circle $w$. Let $w_a,w_b,w_c,w_d,w_e$ be the reflections of $w$ in the sides $AB,BC,CD,DE,EA$, respectively. Let $A'$ be the second intersection point of $w_a$ and $w_e$, and define $B',C',D',E'$ similarly. Prove that $$2\le \frac{S_{A'B'C'D'E'}}{S_{ABCDE}}\le 3,$$ where $S_X$ denotes the area of the figure $X$.

Is it possible to write $\binom{n}{2}$ consecutive natural numbers on the edges of a complete graph with $n$ vertices in such a way that for every path (or cycle) of length $3$ whose edges carry the numbers $a,b,c$ (with edge $b$ between edges $a$ and $c$), $b$ is divisible by the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $c$?

Let $g(x)$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ with all coefficients positive. Find all functions $f:\mathbb R^+ \to \mathbb R^+$ such that $$f(f(x)+g(x)+2y)=f(x)+g(x)+2f(y) \quad \text{for all } x,y\in \mathbb R^+.$$

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. Consider circles $w_1$ and $w_2$ such that $w_1$ is tangent to the segments $AB$ and $AD$, and $w_2$ is tangent to the segments $BC$ and $CD$. Suppose that there exists a circle which is tangent to the lines $AD$ and $DC$ and externally tangent to $w_1$ and $w_2$. Prove that there exists a circle which is tangent to the lines $AB$ and $BC$ and also externally tangent to the circles $w_1$ and $w_2$.
For positive reals $a,b,c$ with $ab+bc+ca=1$, show that $$\sqrt{3}\left(\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}+\sqrt{c}\right)\le \frac{a\sqrt{a}}{bc}+\frac{b\sqrt{b}}{ca}+\frac{c\sqrt{c}}{ab}.$$

Points $A$ and $B$ lie on a circle $\omega$ with center $O$ such that $\frac{\pi}{3}< \angle AOB <\frac{2\pi}{3}$. Let $C$ be the circumcenter of triangle $AOB$, and let $l$ be a line through $C$ making an angle of $\frac{\pi}{3}$ with the segment $OC$. The line $l$ meets the tangents to $\omega$ at $A$ and $B$ at $M$ and $N$, respectively. The circumcircles of triangles $CAM$ and $CBN$ meet $\omega$ again at $Q$ and $R$, respectively, and meet each other again at $P$ (other than $C$). Prove that $OP\perp QR$.

We call a set $B$ of natural numbers loyal if there exist natural numbers $i\le j$ such that $B=\{i,i+1,\ldots,j\}$. Let $Q$ be the set of all loyal sets. For every subset $A=\{a_1<a_2<\ldots<a_k\}$ of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ set $$f(A)=\max_{1\le i \le k-1}(a_{i+1}-a_i)\qquad\text{and}\qquad g(A)=\max_{B\subseteq A,\ B\in Q} |B|,$$ and define $$F(n)=\sum_{A\subseteq \{1,2,\ldots,n\}} f(A)\qquad\text{and}\qquad G(n)=\sum_{A\subseteq \{1,2,\ldots,n\}} g(A).$$ Prove that there exists $m\in \mathbb N$ such that $F(n)>G(n)$ for every natural number $n>m$. (Here $|A|$ is the number of elements of $A$, and $f(A)=0$ if $|A|\le 1$.)

Consider a regular $2^k$-gon with center $O$ and label its sides clockwise by $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_{2^k}$. Reflect $O$ in $l_1$, then reflect the resulting point in $l_2$, and continue in this way up to the last side. Prove that the distance between the final point and $O$ is less than the perimeter of the $2^k$-gon.

Do there exist $2000$ real numbers (not necessarily distinct), not all zero, such that whenever any $1000$ of them are taken as the roots of a monic polynomial of degree $1000$, the coefficients of the resulting polynomial (except the coefficient of $x^{1000}$) are a permutation of the $1000$ remaining numbers?
Find all integers $x$ and $y$ such that $$(y^3+xy-1)(x^2+x-y)=(x^3-xy+1)(y^2+x-y).$$

Let $p$ be an odd prime number. A polynomial $f(x)=\sum_{j=0}^n a_jx^j$ with integer coefficients is called $i$-remainder if $\sum_{p-1\mid j,\ j>0}a_j\equiv i\pmod{p}$. Prove that $\{f(0),f(1),\ldots,f(p-1)\}$ is a complete residue system modulo $p$ if and only if the polynomials $f(x), (f(x))^2,\ldots,(f(x))^{p-2}$ are $0$-remainder and the polynomial $(f(x))^{p-1}$ is $1$-remainder.

Let $n$ be a natural number. Suppose $A$ and $B$ are two sets, each containing $n$ points in the plane, such that no three points of a set are collinear. Let $T(A)$ be the number of broken lines with $n-1$ segments which do not intersect themselves and whose vertices are the points of $A$. Define $T(B)$ similarly. If the points of $B$ are the vertices of a convex $n$-gon (are in convex position) but the points of $A$ are not, prove that $T(B)<T(A)$.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of an acute triangle $ABC$. Points $A',B',C'$ on the sides $BC,CA,AB$ are such that the circumcircles of triangles $AB'C'$, $BC'A'$ and $CA'B'$ pass through $O$. Let $\ell_a$ be the radical axis of the circle with center $B'$ and radius $B'C$ and the circle with center $C'$ and radius $C'B$. Define $\ell_b$ and $\ell_c$ similarly. Prove that the lines $\ell_a,\ell_b,\ell_c$ form a triangle whose orthocenter coincides with the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$.

In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$, and let $J$ and $I$ be the excenters opposite the side $AH$ in the triangles $ABH$ and $ACH$. If $P$ is the point where the incircle of $ABC$ touches $BC$, prove that $I,J,P,H$ are concyclic.
Find the maximum number of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that for any two of them, $A$ and $B$, if $A\subset B$ then $|B\setminus A|\geq 3$.

For nonnegative integers $m$ and $n$ define the numbers $a(m,n)$ as follows: $a(0,0)=2$, and for every natural number $n$, $a(0,n)=1$ and $a(n,0)=2$; for $m,n\geq1$ $$a(m,n)=a(m-1,n)+a(m,n-1).$$ Prove that for every natural number $k$ all the roots of the polynomial $P_k(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{k}a(i,2k+1-2i)x^i$ are real.

Let $m$ and $n$ be two nonnegative integers. In Philosopher's Chess, the board is an infinite grid of identical regular hexagons, and a new piece named the Donkey moves on it as follows: starting from a hexagon, the Donkey moves $m$ cells in one of the $6$ directions, then turns $60^\circ$ clockwise and moves $n$ cells in this new direction, reaching its final cell. At most how many cells can be chosen on the board such that one cannot go from any one of them to another by a finite number of moves of the Donkey?
Do there exist natural numbers $a, b, c$ such that $a^2+b^2+c^2$ is divisible by $2013(ab+bc+ca)$?

Points $A, B, C, D$ lie on a line $l$ in this order. Two circular arcs $C_1$ and $C_2$, both lying on one side of $l$, pass through $A$ and $B$, and two circular arcs $C_3$ and $C_4$ pass through $C$ and $D$, such that $C_1$ is tangent to $C_3$ and $C_2$ is tangent to $C_4$. Prove that the common external tangent of $C_2$ and $C_3$ and the common external tangent of $C_1$ and $C_4$ meet on the line $l$.

Nonnegative real numbers $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ and $q_1,\ldots,q_n$ satisfy $p_1+\cdots+p_n=q_1+\cdots+q_n$. Among all matrices with nonnegative entries in which the sum of the entries of the $i$-th row is $p_i$ and the sum of the entries of the $j$-th column is $q_j$, find the maximum possible sum of the entries on the main diagonal.

Find all arithmetic progressions $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of natural numbers for which there exists a natural number $N>1$ such that for every $k\in \mathbb{N}$ $$a_1a_2\cdots a_k\mid a_{N+1}a_{N+2}\cdots a_{N+k}.$$
Find all functions $f,g:\mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ such that $f$ is increasing and $$f(f(x)+2g(x)+3f(y))=g(x)+2f(x)+3g(y),$$ $$g(f(x)+y+g(y))=2x-g(x)+f(y)+y.$$

On each edge of a graph a real number is written, such that for every closed tour of even length in this graph, the sum of its edge numbers taken with alternating signs $+$ and $-$ is zero. Prove that one can assign a real number to each vertex of the graph such that the sum of the numbers at two adjacent vertices equals the number on the edge between them. (A tour is a closed path along edges of the graph which may repeat edges or vertices.)
Let $a,b,c$ be the sides of a triangle with $a\geq b \geq c$. Prove that $$\sqrt{a(a+b-\sqrt{ab})}+\sqrt{b(a+c-\sqrt{ac})}+\sqrt{c(b+c-\sqrt{bc})}\geq a+b+c.$$

Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral inscribed in a circle $\omega$. Let $I_1,I_2$ and $r_1,r_2$ be the incenters and inradii of triangles $ACD$ and $ABC$, respectively, and assume $r_1=r_2$. Let $\omega'$ be a circle which touches $AB$, $AD$ and touches $\omega$ at $T$. The tangents to $\omega$ at $A$ and $T$ meet at $K$. Prove that $I_1,I_2,K$ are collinear.

$P$ is an arbitrary point inside an acute triangle $ABC$. Let $A_1,B_1,C_1$ be the reflections of $P$ in the sides $BC,CA,AB$. Prove that the centroid of triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ lies inside triangle $ABC$.
We are given $n$ rectangles in the plane. Prove that among the $4n$ right angles formed by these rectangles there are at least $\lfloor 4\sqrt n\rfloor$ distinct right angles.

(a) Does there exist a sequence $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ of positive integers and a positive integer $N$ such that for all $m>N$, $a_m$ has exactly $d(m)-1$ divisors among the $a_i$?

(b) Does there exist a sequence $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ of positive integers and a positive integer $N$ such that for all $m>N$, $a_m$ has exactly $d(m)+1$ divisors among the $a_i$?

Here $d(m)$ is the number of positive divisors of $m$.

The function $f:\mathbb Z \to \mathbb Z$ has the property that for all integers $m$ and $n$ $$f(m)+f(n)+f(f(m^2+n^2))=1.$$ We know that there are integers $a$ and $b$ with $f(a)-f(b)=3$. Prove that there are integers $c$ and $d$ such that $f(c)-f(d)=1$.

In a triangle $ABC$, $AD$ and $AH$ are the angle bisector and the altitude from $A$, respectively. The perpendicular bisector of $AD$ meets the semicircles with diameters $AB$ and $AC$, drawn outside triangle $ABC$, at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that the quadrilateral $XYDH$ is cyclic.

A special parallelogram tile is made by attaching two right isosceles triangles with legs of length $1$ along a leg. We want to put some of these tiles on the floor of an $n\times n$ room such that the distance from each vertex of each tile to the sides of the room is an integer and no two tiles overlap. Prove that an area of at least $n$ of the room is not covered by tiles.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of an acute triangle $ABC$, and let $w$ be the circle with center $O$ tangent to $BC$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be the intersections of the tangents from $A$ to $w$ with the line $BC$ ($X$ and $B$ on the same side of $AO$). $T$ is the intersection of the tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $B$ and the line through $X$ parallel to $AC$; $S$ is the intersection of the tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $C$ and the line through $Y$ parallel to $AB$. Prove that $ST$ is tangent to the circumcircle of $ABC$.
Find all polynomials $P$ with integer coefficients such that $P(\mathbb{Z})=\{P(a):a\in \mathbb{Z}\}$ contains an infinite geometric progression.

Number the rows and columns of an $n\times n$ table by $0,1,\ldots,n-1$ (from left to right and from top to bottom). The table is called selfish if for all $i,j\in\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$ the number in the cell $(i,j)$ is equal to the number of occurrences of the number $i$ in row $j$. For example, the following table is selfish for $n=5$: $$\begin{array}{ccccc}1&0&3&3&4\\1&3&2&1&1\\0&1&0&1&0\\2&1&0&0&0\\1&0&0&0&0\end{array}$$ Prove that there is no selfish table for $n>5$.

Find the minimum number of permutations of the set $\{1,2,3,\ldots,2014\}$ such that for any two different numbers $a$ and $b$ of this set, in at least one of the permutations $b$ comes immediately after $a$.

Let $n$ be a natural number. Prove that for all positive real numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1}$ with $x_1x_2\cdots x_{n+1}=1$ $$\sqrt[x_1]{n}+\cdots+\sqrt[x_{n+1}]{n} \geq n^{\sqrt[n]{x_1}}+\cdots+n^{\sqrt[n]{x_{n+1}}}.$$

$I$ is the incenter of a triangle $ABC$. The perpendicular to $AI$ at $I$ meets $AB$ and $AC$ at $B'$ and $C'$, respectively. Points $B''$ and $C''$ on the half-lines $BC$ and $CB$ are such that $BB''=BA$ and $CC''=CA$. Let $T$ be the second intersection of the circumcircles of $AB'B''$ and $AC'C''$. Prove that the circumcenter of $AIT$ lies on $BC$.

Consider a tree with $n$ vertices labeled $1,\ldots,n$, no label being used twice. We change the labeling as follows: each time we pick an edge that has not been picked before and swap the labels of its endpoints. After performing this action $n-1$ times, we obtain a labeling which is a permutation of the original one. Prove that this permutation consists of exactly one cycle.

Point $D$ is an arbitrary point on the side $BC$ of triangle $ABC$. $I$, $I_1$ and $I_2$ are the incenters of triangles $ABC$, $ABD$ and $ACD$, respectively. $M\neq A$ and $N\neq A$ are the second intersections of the circumcircle of $ABC$ with the circumcircles of $IAI_1$ and $IAI_2$, respectively. Prove that, regardless of the point $D$, the line $MN$ passes through a fixed point.
Prove that for every $k> 1$ the equation $(x+1)(x+2)\cdots(x+k)=y^2$ has finitely many solutions.

Let $n$ be a natural number. A permutation $a_1,\dots,a_n$ of $1,\dots,n$ is called quadratic (cubic) if $a_ia_{i+1}+1$ is a perfect square (cube) for all $1\leq i \leq n-1$.

(a) Prove that for infinitely many natural numbers $n$ there exists a quadratic permutation.

(b) Prove that for no natural number $n$ does a cubic permutation exist.
Let $x,y,z>0$ be real numbers such that $x^2+y^2+z^2=x^2y^2+y^2z^2+z^2x^2$. Prove that $$\left((x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\right)^2\leq 2\left((x^2-y^2)^2+(y^2-z^2)^2+(z^2-x^2)^2\right).$$

Consider $n$ segments in the plane, no two of which intersect, such that no three of their $2n$ endpoints are collinear. Is the following statement true?

Statement: there exists a simple $2n$-gon whose vertices are the $2n$ endpoints of the segments and such that each segment lies completely inside the polygon or is a side of the polygon.

The incircle, with center $I$, of a non-isosceles triangle $ABC$ touches the sides $BC,AC,AB$ at $A_1,B_1,C_1$. The lines $AI,BI,CI$ meet $BC,AC,AB$ at $A_2,B_2,C_2$. Let $A'$ be the point on $AI$ such that $A_1A'\perp B_2C_2$, and define $B',C'$ similarly. Prove that the triangles $A'B'C'$ and $A_1B_1C_1$ are congruent.

Let $m,n\in \mathbb{N}$ and let $p(x),q(x),h(x)$ be polynomials with real coefficients such that $p(x)$ is decreasing and for all $x\in \mathbb{R}$ $$p(q(nx+m)+h(x))=n(q(p(x))+h(x))+m.$$ Prove that there is no function $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x\in \mathbb{R}$ $$f(q(p(x))+h(x))=f(x)^2+1.$$
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}^+\to \mathbb{R}^+$ such that for all $x,y\in \mathbb{R}^+$ $$f\left(\frac{y}{f(x+1)}\right)+f\left(\frac{x+1}{xf(y)}\right)=f(y).$$

A set $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$ of natural numbers is given in which $1\leq x_i-x_{i-1}\leq 2$ for all $1< i \leq n$. A real number $a$ is called good if there exists $1\leq j \leq n$ such that $2|x_j-a|\leq 1$. A subset of $X$ is called compact if the average of its elements is a good number. Prove that at least $2^{n-3}$ subsets of $X$ are compact.

The incircle, with center $I$, of a non-isosceles triangle $ABC$ touches the side $BC$ at $D$. Let $X$ be a point on the arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ such that, if $E,F$ are the feet of the perpendiculars from $X$ to $BI,CI$ and $M$ is the midpoint of $EF$, then $MB=MC$. Prove that $\angle BAD=\angle CAX$.
Find all polynomials $P,Q\in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ such that $$P(x)^3+Q(x)^3=x^{12}+1.$$

$I_b$ is the $B$-excenter of a triangle $ABC$ and $\omega$ is its circumcircle. $M$ is the midpoint of the arc $BC$ of $\omega$ not containing $A$. $MI_b$ meets $\omega$ again at $T\neq M$. Prove that $$TB\cdot TC=TI_b^2.$$
Let $b_1<b_2<b_3<\cdots$ be the sequence of all natural numbers which are sums of squares of two natural numbers. Prove that there exist infinitely many natural numbers $m$ with $b_{m+1}-b_m=2015$.
Let $n$ be a fixed natural number. Find the least $k$ such that every set $A$ of $k$ natural numbers has a subset with an even number of elements the sum of whose members is divisible by $n$.

Let $A$ be a set of edges of an $n\times n$ table. Let $V(A)$ be the set of vertices of the table which are endpoints of at least one edge of $A$, and let $j(A)$ be the number of connected components of the graph $G$ with vertex set $V(A)$ and edge set $A$. Prove that for every natural number $l$ $$\frac{l}{2}\leq \min_{|A|\geq l}\left(|V(A)|-j(A)\right) \leq \frac{l}{2}+\sqrt{\frac{l}{2}}+1.$$

$ABCD$ is a quadrilateral which is both inscribed and circumscribed, and $O$ is its circumcenter. $E,F,S$ are the intersections of $AB$ and $CD$, $AD$ and $BC$, $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. $E'$ and $F'$ are points on $AD$ and $AB$ such that $\angle AEE'=\angle E'ED$ and $\angle AFF'=\angle F'FB$. $X$ and $Y$ are points on $OE'$ and $OF'$ such that $\frac{XA}{XD}=\frac{EA}{ED}$ and $\frac{YA}{YB}=\frac{FA}{FB}$. $M$ is the midpoint of the arc $BD$ of the circumcircle which contains $A$. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $OXY$ and $OAM$ and the circle with diameter $OS$ are coaxal.

Positive numbers $a,b,c,d$ satisfy $\frac{1}{ab}+\frac{1}{bc}+\frac{1}{cd}+\frac{1}{da}=1$. Prove that $$abcd+16 \geq 8 \sqrt{(a+c)\left(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{c}\right)}+8\sqrt{(b+d)\left(\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{d}\right)}.$$

In a triangle $ABC$ with incenter $I$, the line through $A$ parallel to $BC$ meets the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $A_1$. Let $D=AI\cap BC$ and let $E$ be the point where the incircle touches $BC$. The line $EA_1$ meets the circumcircle of triangle $ADE$ again at $T$. Prove that $AI=TI$.
Find the maximum number of rectangles with sides $1$ and $2$ parallel to the coordinate axes such that any two of them have a common part of area $1$.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle. Point $Z$ is on the altitude from $A$, and points $X$ and $Y$ are on the altitudes from $B$ and $C$, outside the triangle, such that $\angle AYB=\angle BZC=\angle CXA=90^\circ$. Prove that $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ are collinear if and only if the length of the tangent from $A$ to the nine-point circle of $ABC$ is equal to the sum of the lengths of the tangents from $B$ and $C$ to the nine-point circle of $ABC$.

A permutation $(a_1, a_2,\ldots , a_n)$ of the set $\{1,2,\ldots, n\}$ is called good if $n\nmid a_i+a_k-2a_j$ for any three natural numbers $i <j <k$. Find all natural numbers $n\ge 3$ for which there exists a good permutation of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$.

If $a,b,c$ are positive real numbers such that $a+b+c=abc$, prove that $$\frac{abc}{3\sqrt{2}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{a^3+b^3}}{ab+1}+\frac{\sqrt{b^3+c^3}}{bc+1}+\frac{\sqrt{c^3+a^3}}{ca+1}\right)\geq \frac{a}{a^2+1}+\frac{b}{b^2+1}+\frac{c}{c^2+1}.$$

Point $A$ lies outside a given circle $\omega$. The tangents from $A$ to $\omega$ touch it at $S$ and $T$, and $X, Y$ are the midpoints of $AT$ and $AS$. The tangent from $X$ to $\omega$ other than $XT$ touches $\omega$ at $R$. Points $P, Q$ are the midpoints of $XT$ and $XR$. Let $K=XY\cap PQ$ and $L=SX\cap TK$. Prove that the quadrilateral $KRLQ$ is cyclic.

Let $a_1, a_2, a_3$ be three given positive integers, and consider the sequence $$a_{n+1}=\operatorname{lcm}[a_n, a_{n-1}]-\operatorname{lcm}[a_{n-1}, a_{n-2}]\quad\text{for } n\ge 3.$$ Prove that there exists a positive integer $k\le a_3+4$ such that $a_k\le 0$. (Since $\operatorname{lcm}$ is defined only for nonzero integers, the sequence is defined until a term equal to zero appears.)

$a_1,a_2,\ldots ,a_n,b_1,b_2,\ldots ,b_n$ are $2n$ positive real numbers such that $a_1,a_2,\ldots ,a_n$ are not all equal and can be divided into two subsets with equal sums, and similarly $b_1,b_2,\ldots ,b_n$ satisfy the same two conditions. Prove that there exists a simple $2n$-gon with sides parallel to the coordinate axes whose horizontal sides have lengths $a_1,a_2,\ldots ,a_n$ and whose vertical sides have lengths $b_1,b_2,\ldots ,b_n$. (A simple polygon is a polygon which does not intersect itself.)

Ali puts $5$ points in the plane such that no three of them are collinear. Ramtin adds a sixth point that is not collinear with any two of the former points. Ali then wants to form two triangles with vertices among the six points such that one can be placed inside the other. Can Ali place the $5$ points so that he will always be able to construct the desired triangles? (A triangle $T_1$ can be placed inside a triangle $T_2$ if $T_1$ is congruent to a triangle lying completely inside $T_2$.)

Prove that for each natural number $d$ there is a unique monic polynomial $P$ of degree $d$ with $P(1)\neq 0$ such that for every sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of real numbers satisfying $$P(n)a_1 + P(n-1)a_2 + \cdots + P(1)a_n=0\quad\text{for all } n>1$$ there is a natural number $k$ with $0=a_k=a_{k+1}= \cdots$.

$AH$ is the altitude of a triangle $ABC$ and $H'$ is the reflection of $H$ in the midpoint of $BC$. The tangents to the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $B$ and $C$ meet at $X$, and the line through $H'$ perpendicular to $XH'$ meets $AB$ and $AC$ at $Y$ and $Z$, respectively. Prove that $\angle ZXC=\angle YXB$.

Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers with $m>n$. Define $x_k=\frac{m+k}{n+k}$ for $k=1,2,\ldots,n+1$. Prove that if all the numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1}$ are integers, then $x_1x_2\cdots x_{n+1}-1$ is divisible by an odd prime.

For a finite set $A$ of positive integers, a partition of $A$ into two disjoint nonempty subsets $A_1$ and $A_2$ is called good if the least common multiple of the elements of $A_1$ is equal to the greatest common divisor of the elements of $A_2$. Determine the minimum value of $n$ such that there exists a set of $n$ positive integers with exactly $2015$ good partitions.

Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral, and let $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ be points on the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$, respectively. Let the segments $PR$ and $QS$ meet at $O$. Suppose that each of the quadrilaterals $APOS$, $BQOP$, $CROQ$ and $DSOR$ has an incircle. Prove that the lines $AC$, $PQ$ and $RS$ are either concurrent or parallel to each other.
Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. Find the maximum possible value of $$\sum_{1 \le r < s \le 2n} (s-r-n)x_rx_s,$$ where $-1 \le x_i \le 1$ for all $i = 1, \ldots , 2n$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle C = 90^{\circ}$, and let $H$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$. A point $D$ is chosen inside the triangle $CBH$ so that $CH$ bisects $AD$. Let $P$ be the intersection point of the lines $BD$ and $CH$. Let $\omega$ be the semicircle with diameter $BD$ that meets the segment $CB$ at an interior point. A line through $P$ is tangent to $\omega$ at $Q$. Prove that the lines $CQ$ and $AD$ meet on $\omega$.

In a company of people some pairs are enemies. A group of people is called unsociable if the number of its members is odd and at least $3$, and it is possible to arrange all its members around a round table so that every two neighbors are enemies. Given that there are at most $2015$ unsociable groups, prove that it is possible to partition the company into $11$ parts so that no two enemies are in the same part.

Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle and let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$. A circle $\omega$ passing through $B$ and $M$ meets the sides $AB$ and $BC$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $T$ be the point such that $BPTQ$ is a parallelogram. Suppose that $T$ lies on the circumcircle of $ABC$. Determine all possible values of $\frac{BT}{BM}$.

Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive real numbers such that $\frac{1}{a+1}+\frac{1}{b+1}+\frac{1}{c+1}+\frac{1}{d+1}=2$. Prove that $$\sqrt{\frac{a^2+1}{2}}+\sqrt{\frac{b^2+1}{2}}+\sqrt{\frac{c^2+1}{2}}+\sqrt{\frac{d^2+1}{2}} \geq 3\left(\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}+\sqrt{c}+\sqrt{d}\right) -8.$$

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $CA \neq CB$. Let $D$, $F$, $G$ be the midpoints of the sides $AB$, $AC$, $BC$, respectively. A circle $\Gamma$ passing through $C$ and tangent to $AB$ at $D$ meets the segments $AF$ and $BG$ at $H$ and $I$, respectively. The points $H'$ and $I'$ are symmetric to $H$ and $I$ about $F$ and $G$, respectively. The line $H'I'$ meets $CD$ and $FG$ at $Q$ and $M$, respectively. The line $CM$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $P$. Prove that $CQ = QP$.

Let $P$ and $P'$ be two non-congruent regular $n$-gons, and $A$ and $A'$ points inside $P$ and $P'$, respectively. Let $\{ d_1 , d_2 , \ldots, d_n \}$ be the distances from $A$ to the vertices of $P$, and define $\{ d'_1 , d'_2 , \ldots, d'_n \}$ similarly for $P'$ and $A'$. Is it possible for $\{ d'_1 , d'_2 , \ldots, d'_n \}$ to be a permutation of $\{ d_1 , d_2 , \ldots, d_n \}$?

Let $\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ denote the set of positive integers. For any positive integer $k$, a function $f: \mathbb{Z}_{>0} \to \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ is called $k$-good if $\gcd(f(m) + n, f(n) + m) \le k$ for all $m \neq n$. Find all $k$ such that there exists a $k$-good function.

A real function is assigned to every cell of an $n \times n$ table. Prove that a function can be assigned to each row and each column of this table such that the function assigned to each cell is equal to the composition of the functions assigned to the row and the column containing it.

Let $ABC$ be an arbitrary triangle and $O$ its circumcenter. Points $X,Y$ lie on $AB,AC$, respectively, such that the reflection of $BC$ in $XY$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $AXY$. Prove that the circumcircle of triangle $AXY$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $BOC$.

Let $p \neq 13$ be a prime number of the form $8k+5$ such that $39$ is a quadratic non-residue modulo $p$. Prove that the congruence $$x_1^4+x_2^4+x_3^4+x_4^4 \equiv 0 \pmod p$$ has a solution in integers with $p\nmid x_1x_2x_3x_4$.

Suppose that a sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of positive real numbers satisfies $$a_{k+1}\geq\frac{ka_k}{a_k^2+(k-1)}$$ for every positive integer $k$. Prove that $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n\geq n$ for every $n\geq2$.

Let $AD,BF,CE$ be the altitudes of a triangle $ABC$. $Q$ is a point on the line $EF$ such that $QF=DE$ and $F$ is between $E$ and $Q$. $P$ is a point on the line $EF$ such that $EP=DF$ and $E$ is between $P$ and $F$. The perpendicular bisector of $DQ$ meets $AB$ at $X$, and the perpendicular bisector of $DP$ meets $AC$ at $Y$. Prove that the midpoint of $BC$ lies on $XY$.

A council consists of five members, and decisions in this council are made by a method based on the positive or negative votes of its members. The method has the following two properties:

• Monotonicity: if the final decision is favorable and one of the opposing members changes his or her vote, the final decision will still be favorable.

• Symmetry: if all of the members change their votes, the final decision changes too.

Prove that the council uses a weighted decision method; that is, nonnegative weights $\omega_1 , \omega_2 , \ldots ,\omega_5$ can be assigned to the members of the council such that the final decision is favorable if and only if the sum of the weights of those in favor is greater than the sum of the weights of the rest.
Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive real numbers with $a+b+c+d=2$. Prove that $$\frac{(a+c)^2}{ad+bc}+\frac{(b+d)^2}{ac+bd}+4\geq 4\left( \frac{a+b+1}{c+d+1}+\frac{c+d+1}{a+b+1} \right).$$

In the country of Sugarland there are $13$ students in the IMO team selection camp. Six team selection tests were taken and the results have come out; no two students have the same score on the same test. To select the IMO team, the national committee has decided to choose a permutation of these $6$ tests and, starting from the first test, the student with the highest score among the remaining students on that test becomes a member of the team. The committee is having a session to choose the permutation. Is it possible that all $13$ students have a chance of becoming a team member?

In a triangle $ABC$ let $I_a$ be the $A$-excenter. Let $\omega$ be an arbitrary circle that passes through $A$ and $I_a$ and meets the extensions of the sides $AB,AC$ (beyond $B,C$) at $X,Y$, respectively. Let $S,T$ be points on the segments $I_aB,I_aC$, respectively, such that $\angle AXI_a=\angle BTI_a$ and $\angle AYI_a=\angle CSI_a$. The lines $BT,CS$ meet at $K$, and the lines $KI_a,TS$ meet at $Z$. Prove that $X,Y,Z$ are collinear.

Arrange all prime numbers in increasing order: $p_1=2<p_2<p_3<\cdots$. Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be a sequence of positive integers such that for all $i=1,2,3,\ldots$ the congruence $x^{n_i} \equiv 2 \pmod {p_i}$ has a solution $x$. Is there always a number $x$ that satisfies all these congruences?

In a triangle $ABC$, points $P,Q$ lie on the side $BC$ such that $BP=CQ$ and $P$ lies between $B$ and $Q$. The circumcircle of triangle $APQ$ meets the sides $AB,AC$ at $E,F$, respectively. $T$ is the intersection of $EP$ and $FQ$. The two lines through the midpoint of $BC$ parallel to $AB$ and $AC$ meet $EP$ and $FQ$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircles of triangles $TXY$ and $APQ$ are tangent to each other.

In the unit squares of a transparent $1 \times 100$ tape the numbers $1,2,\ldots,100$ are written in increasing order. We fold the tape along its lines, in arbitrary order and arbitrary directions, until we obtain a $1 \times 1$ tape with $100$ layers. A permutation of the numbers $1,2,\ldots,100$ can then be read on the tape from top to bottom. Prove that the number of possible permutations is between $2^{100}$ and $4^{100}$. (For example, all permutations of the numbers $1,2,3$ can be produced with a $1\times3$ tape.)

$ABCD$ is a trapezoid with $AB \parallel CD$ whose diagonals meet at $P$. Let $\omega_1$ be a circle passing through $B$ and tangent to $AC$ at $A$, and $\omega_2$ a circle passing through $C$ and tangent to $BD$ at $D$. $\omega_3$ is the circumcircle of triangle $BPC$. Prove that the common chord of the circles $\omega_1,\omega_3$ and the common chord of the circles $\omega_2, \omega_3$ meet on $AD$.
Find the largest number $n$ for which there exist $n$ positive integers such that none of them divides another, but among any three of them one divides the sum of the other two.

There are $27$ cards; each card shows $1$, $2$ or $3$ copies of one shape (a circle, a square or a triangle) in one color (white, grey or black), and all $27$ combinations occur. A triple of cards is called a match if the three cards have either the same number of shapes or three distinct numbers of shapes, either the same shape or three distinct shapes, and either the same color or three distinct colors. For instance, three cards with distinct numbers of shapes, distinct shapes and the same color form a match. What is the maximum number of cards that can be chosen so that no three of them form a match?

An $(n+1)$-tuple $\left(h_1,h_2, \ldots, h_{n+1}\right)$ of polynomials $h_i(x_1,x_2, \ldots , x_n)$ in $n$ variables with real coefficients is called good if the following condition holds: for any $n$ functions $f_1,f_2, \ldots ,f_n : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$, if $P_i(x)=h_i \left(f_1(x),f_2(x), \ldots, f_n(x) \right)$ is a polynomial in $x$ for all $1 \le i \le n+1$, then $f_1(x),f_2(x), \ldots, f_n(x)$ are polynomials.

(a) Prove that for all positive integers $n$ there exists a good $(n+1)$-tuple $\left(h_1,h_2, \ldots, h_{n+1}\right)$ such that the degree of every $h_i$ is greater than $1$.

(b) Prove that there is no integer $n>1$ for which there is a good $(n+1)$-tuple $\left(h_1,h_2, \ldots, h_{n+1}\right)$ of symmetric polynomials.

Let $k,n$ be two arbitrary positive integers. Prove that there exist at least $(k-1)(n-k+1)$ positive integers that can be produced from $n$ copies of the number $k$ using only the operations $+,-,\times, \div$ and parentheses, but cannot be produced using $n-1$ copies of $k$.

Let $k>1$ be an integer. The sequence $a_1,a_2, \ldots$ is defined by $a_1=1$, $a_2=k$ and $a_{n+1}-(k+1)a_n+a_{n-1}=0$ for all $n>1$. Find all positive integers $n$ such that $a_n$ is a power of $k$.

Let $n>1$ be an integer. Prove that there exists an integer $m$ with $n-1 \ge m \ge \left \lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right \rfloor$ such that the following equation has an integer solution with $a_m>0$: $$\frac{a_m}{m+1}+\frac{a_{m+1}}{m+2}+ \cdots + \frac{a_{n-1}}{n}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{lcm}\left( 1,2, \ldots , n \right)}.$$

Let $P$ be a point in the interior of a quadrilateral $ABCD$ such that $$\angle BPC=2\angle BAC,\quad \angle PCA = \angle PAD,\quad \angle PDA=\angle PAC.$$ Prove that $$\angle PBD= \left| \angle BCA - \angle PCA \right|.$$

Find all functions $f: \mathbb{R}^+ \times \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ that satisfy the following conditions for all positive real numbers $x,y,z$: $$f\left( f(x,y),z \right)=x^2y^2f(x,z),$$ $$f\left( x,1+f(x,y) \right) \ge x^2 + xyf(x,x).$$

There are $6$ points in the plane such that no three of them are collinear. It is known that among any $4$ of them there is a point whose power with respect to the circle through the other three points is a constant value $k$. (The power of a point inside a circle is negative.) Prove that $k=0$ and that all $6$ points lie on a circle.

Let $(c_i)_{i=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of non-negative real numbers with $c_{2017}>0$. A sequence of polynomials is defined by $$P_{-1}(x)=0, \quad P_0(x)=1, \quad P_{n+1}(x)=xP_n(x)+c_nP_{n-1}(x).$$ Prove that there is no integer $n>2017$ and real number $c$ such that $$P_{2n}(x)=P_n(x^2+c).$$

In a triangle $ABC$ let $O$ and $H$ be the circumcenter and the orthocenter. The point $P$ is the reflection of $A$ in $OH$. Assume that $P$ is not on the same side of $BC$ as $A$. Points $E,F$ lie on $AB,AC$, respectively, such that $BE=PC$ and $CF=PB$. Let $K$ be the intersection point of $AP$ and $OH$. Prove that $\angle EKF = 90^{\circ}$.

Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots , A_k$ be subsets of $\{1,2,3,\ldots,n\}$ such that $A_i\cap A_j \neq \varnothing$ for all $1\leq i,j\leq k$. Prove that there are $n$ distinct positive integers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ such that for each $1\leq j\leq k$ $$\operatorname{lcm}_{i \in A_j}\{x_i\}>\operatorname{lcm}_{i \notin A_j}\{x_i\}.$$

Determine the least real number $k$ such that the inequality $$\left(\frac{2a}{a-b}\right)^2+\left(\frac{2b}{b-c}\right)^2+\left(\frac{2c}{c-a}\right)^2+k \geq 4\left(\frac{2a}{a-b}+\frac{2b}{b-c}+\frac{2c}{c-a}\right)$$ holds for all real numbers $a,b,c$.

In a triangle $ABC$ let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Let $\omega$ be a circle inside $ABC$ which is tangent to $AB,AC$ at $E,F$, respectively. The tangents from $M$ to $\omega$ touch $\omega$ at $P,Q$ such that $P$ and $B$ lie on the same side of $AM$. Let $X = PM \cap BF$ and $Y = QM \cap CE$. If $2PM=BC$, prove that $XY$ is tangent to $\omega$.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle A\neq 90^\circ$, and let $BE,CF$ be its altitudes. The bisector of $\angle A$ meets $EF$ and $BC$ at $M$ and $N$. Let $P$ be a point such that $MP\perp EF$ and $NP\perp BC$. Prove that $AP$ passes through the midpoint of $BC$.

Prove that for each positive integer $m$ one can find $m$ consecutive positive integers $n$ such that the number $$\left(1^3+2018^3\right)\left(2^3+2018^3\right)\cdots \left(n^3+2018^3\right)$$ is not a perfect power.

A simple graph is called a divisibility graph if it is possible to put distinct numbers on its vertices such that two vertices are joined by an edge if and only if the number of one of them is divisible by the number of the other.

A simple graph with $n$ vertices is called permutationary if it is possible to put the numbers $1,2,\ldots,n$ on its vertices so that there is a permutation $\pi$ such that vertices $i,j$ are joined by an edge if and only if $i>j$ and $\pi(i)< \pi(j)$ (the graph is not directed).

Prove that a simple graph is permutationary if and only if both the graph and its complement are divisibility graphs.

Mojtaba and Hooman play a game. First Mojtaba draws $2018$ vectors with zero sum. Then, in turns starting with Mojtaba, each player takes one of the vectors and places it in the plane; after the first move, each vector must be placed with its beginning at the end of the previous vector. At the end a closed polygon is obtained. If this polygon does not intersect itself, Mojtaba wins; otherwise Hooman wins. Who has a winning strategy?

Let $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ be an infinite sequence of distinct integers. Prove that there are infinitely many primes $p$ for which distinct positive integers $i,j,k$ can be found such that $p\mid a_ia_ja_k-1$.

Call a positive integer useful but not optimized if it can be written as a sum of distinct powers of $3$ and distinct powers of $5$. Prove that there exist infinitely many positive integers which are not useful but not optimized. (For example, $37=(3^0+3^1+3^3)+(5^0+5^1)$ is useful but not optimized.)

Let $\omega$ be the circumcircle of an isosceles triangle $ABC$ with $AB=AC$. Points $P$ and $Q$ lie on $\omega$ and $BC$, respectively, such that $AP=AQ$. $AP$ and $BC$ meet at $R$. Prove that the tangents from $B$ and $C$ to the incircle of triangle $AQR$ (different from $BC$) meet on $\omega$.

$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$ is a sequence of positive integers which contains at least $\frac {2n}{3}+1$ distinct numbers, and in which each positive integer occurs at most three times. Prove that there exists a permutation $b_1,b_2,\ldots,b_n$ of the $a_i$ such that all the $n$ sums $b_i+b_{i+1}$ ($1\le i\le n$, $b_{n+1}=b_1$) are distinct.

Two circles $\omega_1$ with center $O$ and $\omega_2$ meet at $A$ and $B$, and $O$ lies on $\omega_2$. Let $S$ be the point on $AB$ such that $OS\perp AB$. The line $OS$ meets $\omega_2$ again at $P$. The bisector of $\angle ASP$ meets $\omega_1$ at $L$ ($A$ and $L$ on the same side of the line $OP$). Let $K$ be a point on $\omega_2$ such that $PS=PK$ ($A$ and $K$ on the same side of the line $OP$). Prove that $SL=KL$.

Find the maximum possible value of $k$ for which there exist distinct reals $x_1,x_2,\ldots ,x_k$ greater than $1$ such that for all $1 \leq i, j \leq k$ $$x_i^{\lfloor x_j \rfloor }= x_j^{\lfloor x_i\rfloor}.$$

Distinct positive integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots ,a_n$ are called good if their sum is equal to the sum of all pairwise $\gcd$'s among them. Prove that there are infinitely many $n$ for which $n$ good numbers exist.
$2n-1$ distinct positive real numbers with sum $S$ are given. Prove that there are at least $\binom {2n-2}{n-1}$ different ways to choose $n$ of them such that their sum is at least $\frac {S}{2}$.

Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle $\omega$, and $P= AC\cap BD$. Points $E$ and $F$ lie on the sides $AB$ and $CD$, respectively, such that $\angle APE=\angle DPF$. Circles $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ are tangent to $\omega$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively, and both are tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $PEF$ at $P$. Prove that $$\frac {EX}{EY}=\frac {FX}{FY}.$$

A table with $5$ columns and $32$ rows filled with zeros and ones is called varied if no two of its rows are filled in the same way. On the lateral surface of a cylinder a table with $32$ rows and $16$ columns is drawn. Is it possible to fill the cells of this table with zeros and ones so that for any five consecutive columns, the $32\times5$ table formed by these columns is varied?

$a, a_1,a_2,\ldots ,a_n$ are natural numbers. We know that for every natural number $k$ for which $ak+1$ is a perfect square, at least one of $a_1k+1,\ldots ,a_n k+1$ is also a perfect square. Prove that $a$ is one of $a_1,\ldots ,a_n$.

A point $P$ lies inside a parallelogram $ABCD$. The lines through $A,B,C,D$ perpendicular to $PA,PB,PC,PD$, respectively, form a convex quadrilateral $XYZT$. Prove that $S_{XYZT}\geq 2S_{ABCD}$, where $S$ denotes area.

Consider a triangle $ABC$ with orthocenter $H$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the segments $BC$ and $AH$. Point $D$ lies on the line $MH$ so that $AD\parallel BC$, and point $K$ lies on the line $AH$ so that $DNMK$ is cyclic. Points $E$ and $F$ lie on the lines $AC$ and $AB$ such that $\angle EHM=\angle C$ and $\angle FHM=\angle B$. Prove that the points $D,E,F,K$ lie on a circle.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x,y\in \mathbb{R}$ $$f\left(f(x)^2-y^2\right)^2+f(2xy)^2=f\left(x^2+y^2\right)^2.$$

$(a_n)_{n\geq 0}$ and $(b_n)_{n\geq 0}$ are two sequences of digits $a_i,b_i\in \{0,1,2,\ldots,9\}$. There is an integer $M$ such that $a_n,b_n\neq 0$ for all $n\geq M$, and for each $n\geq 0$ $$\left(\overline{a_n\cdots a_1a_0}\right)^2+999 \mid \left(\overline{b_n\cdots b_1b_0}\right)^2+999.$$ Prove that $a_n=b_n$ for all $n\geq 0$. (Here $\overline{x_nx_{n-1}\cdots x_0} = 10^n x_n + \cdots + 10 x_1 + x_0$.)
$S$ is an infinite set of natural numbers, and $$S'=\left\{x^y+y^x: \ x,y\in S,\ x\neq y\right\}.$$ Prove that the set of prime divisors of the elements of $S'$ is also infinite.

In a triangle $ABC$, $\angle A = 60^\circ$. On the sides $AB$ and $AC$ equilateral triangles $ABK$ and $ACL$ are constructed outside triangle $ABC$. $CK$ and $AB$ meet at $S$, $AC$ and $BL$ meet at $R$, and $BL$ and $CK$ meet at $T$. Prove that the radical center of the circumcircles of triangles $BSK$, $CLR$ and $BTC$ lies on the median from $A$ of triangle $ABC$.

Positive integers $m$ and $n$ are given. There are $mn$ people at a party, standing in the shape of an $m\times n$ grid. Some of them are police officers and the rest are guests; some of the guests may be criminals. The goal is to determine whether or not there is a criminal among the guests.

Two people are adjacent if their cells share a side. Every police officer sees the people adjacent to him and knows for each of them whether or not he is a criminal. On the other hand, every criminal threatens exactly one of the people adjacent to him (possibly an officer!) with murder. A threatened officer is so scared that he denies the existence of any criminal among his adjacent people.

Find the least possible number of officers for which they can take positions at the party in such a way that the goal is achievable. (The number of criminals is unknown; it is possible that there are no criminals.)

Let $1<t<2$ be a real number. Prove that for all sufficiently large positive integers $d$ there is a monic polynomial $P(x)$ of degree $d$ all of whose coefficients are $+1$ or $-1$ such that $$\left|P(t)-2019\right| <1.$$

Let $P$ be a simple polygon lying completely inside a circle $C$ of radius $1$, such that $P$ does not pass through the center of $C$. The perimeter of $P$ is $36$. Prove that there is a radius of $C$ which meets $P$ at least $6$ times, or there is a circle concentric with $C$ which has at least $6$ common points with $P$.

For every positive integer $n$ define the set $$S_n = \left\{x^2+ny^2 : x,y \in \mathbb{Z} \right\}.$$ Find all positive integers $n$ for which there exists an element of $S_n$ which does not belong to any of the sets $S_1, S_2,\ldots,S_{n-1}$.
Find all polynomials $P(x,y)$ with real coefficients such that for all real numbers $x,y,z$ $$P(x,2yz)+P(y,2zx)+P(z,2xy)=P(x+y+z,xy+yz+zx).$$

Hesam chose $10$ distinct positive integers and gave all their pairwise $\gcd$'s and pairwise $\operatorname{lcm}$'s (a total of $90$ numbers) to Masoud. Can Masoud always find the original $10$ numbers just by knowing these $90$ numbers?

In a triangle $ABC$, $M,N,P$ are the midpoints of the sides $BC,CA,AB$. Point $K$ lies on the segment $NP$ so that $AK$ bisects $\angle BKC$. The lines $MN$ and $BK$ meet at $E$, and the lines $MP$ and $CK$ meet at $F$. Let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$, and $L$ the second intersection of the circumcircles of triangles $AKH$ and $HEF$. Prove that $MK$, $EF$ and $HL$ are concurrent.

Given an acute triangle $ABC$ with orthocenter $H$, the reflection of its nine-point circle in $AH$ meets the circumcircle at the points $X$ and $Y$. Prove that $AH$ is the external bisector of $\angle XHY$.

A subgraph of the complete graph on $n$ vertices is chosen such that its number of edges is a multiple of $3$ and every vertex has even degree. Prove that a weight can be assigned to each triangle of the complete graph such that for each edge of the chosen subgraph the sum of the weights of the triangles containing that edge equals $1$, and for each edge not in the subgraph this sum equals $0$.
$x,y,z$ are real numbers such that $x+y+z=xy+yz+zx$. Prove that $$\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}+\frac{y}{\sqrt{y^4+y^2+1}}+\frac{z}{\sqrt{z^4+z^2+1}}\geq \frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}.$$

A complete graph with distinct positive edge weights is given in which every triangle is degenerate, that is, the weight of one of its edges is equal to the sum of the other two. Prove that one can assign values to the vertices of this graph such that the weight of each edge is the difference of the values assigned to its endpoints.

Let $O$ be the circumcenter of a triangle $ABC$. Points $D,E$ lie on the sides $AC,AB$, and points $P,Q,R,S$ in the plane are such that $P,C$ and $R,C$ lie on different sides of $AB$, $Q,B$ and $S,B$ lie on different sides of $AC$, $R$ and $S$ lie on the circumcircles of $DAP$ and $EAQ$, respectively, $\triangle BCE \sim \triangle ADQ$ and $\triangle CBD \sim \triangle AEP$ (in that order), and $\angle ARE=\angle ASD=\angle BAC$. If $RS\parallel PQ$, prove that the lines $RE$ and $DS$ meet on $AO$.

A function $g:[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ has the property that for every partition of $[0,1]$ into two nonempty subsets $A,B$, either there exists $x \in A$ with $g(x) \in B$ or there exists $x \in B$ with $g(x) \in A$. Furthermore, $g(x)>x$ for all $x \in [0,1]$. Prove that there exist infinitely many $x \in [0,1]$ with $g(x)=1$.

Given $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, prove that there exist infinitely many pairs of distinct natural numbers $(m,n)$ such that $$n+s(2n)=m+s(2m)\quad\text{and}\quad kn+s(n^2)=km+s(m^2),$$ where $s(n)$ denotes the sum of the digits of $n$.

$n$ positive numbers are given. Is it always possible to find a convex polygon with $n+3$ sides and a triangulation of it such that the lengths of the diagonals used in the triangulation are the given $n$ numbers?

A monic polynomial $P(x) \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is called square-free mod $n$ if there do not exist polynomials $Q(x),R(x) \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $Q$ non-constant and $P(x) \equiv Q(x)^2 R(x) \pmod n$. Given a prime $p$ and an integer $m \geq 2$, find the number of monic polynomials $P(x)$ of degree $m$ with coefficients in $\{0,1,2,\ldots,p-1\}$ which are square-free mod $p$.

Alice and Bob take turns on a $2020\times2020$ board, Alice starting. In each move a player colours a cell that has not been coloured yet and receives as many points as there are already coloured cells in the same row and column. When the whole board is coloured, the points determine the winner. Who has a winning strategy, and what is the maximum difference that he or she can guarantee?

A triangle $ABC$ with circumcircle $\Gamma$ is given. $E$ and $F$ are the feet of the angle bisectors from $B$ and $C$, $I$ is the incenter and $K$ is the intersection of $AI$ and $EF$. Let $T$ be the midpoint of the arc $BAC$. The circle $\Gamma$ meets the $A$-median and the circumcircle of $AEF$ for the second time at $X$ and $S$. Let $S'$ be the reflection of $S$ in $AI$, and $J$ the second intersection of the circumcircle of $AS'K$ with $AX$. Prove that the quadrilateral $TJIX$ is cyclic.

Let $ABC$ be an isosceles triangle ($AB=AC$) with incenter $I$. A circle $\omega$ passes through $C$ and $I$ and is tangent to $AI$. $\omega$ meets $AC$ and the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $Q$ and $D$, respectively. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$ and $N$ the midpoint of $CQ$. Prove that $AD$, $MN$ and $BC$ are concurrent.
Prove that for every positive integer $k>1$ there exists a real number $x$ such that for every positive integer $n<1398$ $$\left\{x^n\right\}<\left\{x^{n-1}\right\} \iff k\mid n.$$

Let $p$ be an odd prime number. Find all $\frac{p-1}2$-tuples $\left(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_{\frac{p-1}2}\right)\in \mathbb{Z}_p^{\frac{p-1}2}$ such that $$\sum_{i = 1}^{\frac{p-1}{2}} x_i \equiv \sum_{i = 1}^{\frac{p-1}{2}} x_i^2 \equiv \cdots \equiv \sum_{i = 1}^{\frac{p-1}{2}} x_i^{\frac{p - 1}{2}} \pmod p.$$

In an acute scalene triangle $ABC$ the external bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets $BC$ at $X$. Let $l_b$ and $l_c$ be the tangents to the circumcircle $(ABC)$ at $B$ and $C$. A line through $X$ meets $l_b$ and $l_c$ at $Y$ and $Z$, respectively. Let $N$ be the second intersection of $(AYB)$ and $(AZC)$, and $D=l_b\cap l_c$. Show that $ND$ is the bisector of the angle $YNZ$.

In a simple connected graph $G$ let $x_i$ be the number of vertices of degree $i$, and let $d>3$ be the largest degree in $G$. Prove that if $$x_d \ge x_{d-1} + 2x_{d-2}+\cdots +(d-1)x_1,$$ then there exists a vertex of degree $d$ whose removal leaves $G$ connected.

Positive integers $a,b,c,d$ with $abcd \neq 1$ are pairwise coprime. Two multiplicative functions $f,g : \mathbb{N} \to \{0,1\}$ satisfy $f(an+b)=g(cn+d)$ for every positive integer $n$. Prove that at least one of the following holds:

(i) $f(an+b)=g(cn+d)=0$ for every positive integer $n$;

(ii) there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $g(n)=f(n)=1$ for all $n$ with $\gcd(n,k)=1$.

(A function $f$ is multiplicative if $f(ab)=f(a)f(b)$ for all natural numbers $a,b$.)

Let $\Omega(n)$ and $\omega(n)$ be the largest and the smallest prime factors of $n$, respectively. Alireza and Amin play a game. First Alireza chooses $1400$ polynomials with integer coefficients. Then Amin chooses $700$ of them; let $A$ be the set of polynomials chosen by Amin and $B$ the set of the remaining polynomials. Amin wins if for all $n$ $$\max_{P \in A}\Omega(P(n)) \ge \min_{P \in B}\omega(P(n)).$$ Who has a winning strategy?

Call a triple of numbers nice if one of them is the average of the other two. Assume that $2k+1$ distinct real numbers have $k^2$ nice triples. Prove that these numbers can be divided into two arithmetic progressions with equal common differences.

A point $D$ is chosen on the Euler line of a triangle $ABC$, inside the triangle. $E,F$ are the points where the lines $BD,CD$ meet $AC,AB$, respectively. Point $X$ on the line $AD$ is such that $\angle EXF =180^\circ - \angle A$, with $A,X$ on the same side of $EF$. If $P$ is the second intersection of the circumcircles of $CXF$ and $BXE$, prove that the lines $XP$ and $EF$ meet on the altitude from $A$.

Natural numbers are placed in the cells of an infinite grid such that the number in each cell is equal to the number of its adjacent cells containing the same number. Find the largest possible number of distinct numbers in the grid. (Two cells are adjacent if they have a common vertex.)
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for any two positive integers $m,n$ $$f(n)+1400m^2\mid n^2+f(f(m)).$$

Prove that there exist two relatively prime polynomials $P(x),Q(x)$ with integer coefficients and a real number $u>0$ such that whenever positive integers $a,b,c,d$ satisfy $$\left|\frac{a}{c}-1\right|^{2021} \le \frac{u}{|d||c|^{1010}}\quad\text{and}\quad \left| \left(\frac{a}{c}\right)^{2020}-\frac{b}{d}\right| \le \frac{u}{|d||c|^{1010}},$$ we have $$bP\left(\frac{a}{c}\right)=dQ\left(\frac{a}{c}\right).$$ (Two polynomials are relatively prime if they have no common root.)
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all positive integers $a,b,c$ $$f(ac)+f(bc)-f(c)f(ab) \ge 1.$$

A point $X$ is chosen inside a quadrilateral $ABCD$, which is not a trapezoid, such that $\angle AXD +\angle BXC=180^\circ$. The bisector of $\angle ABX$ meets the altitude from $D$ of triangle $ADX$ at $K$, and the bisector of $\angle DCX$ meets the altitude from $A$ of triangle $ADX$ at $L$. We know that $BK \perp CX$ and $CL \perp BX$. If the circumcenter of $ADX$ lies on the line $KL$, prove that $KL \perp AD$.

Prove that the $n$-element subsets of a set with $3n$ elements can be colored with $8$ colors in such a way that there are no $3$ subsets $A,B,C$ of the same color with $$|A \cap B| \le 1,\quad |A \cap C| \le 1,\quad |B \cap C| \le 1.$$

Morteza has $100$ sets. At each step Mahdi can choose two distinct sets of them, and Morteza tells him their intersection and union. Find the least number of steps after which Mahdi can determine all of the sets.

For a positive integer $n$, let $\tau(n)$ and $\sigma(n)$ be the number of positive divisors of $n$ and the sum of the positive divisors of $n$, respectively. Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers such that $\sigma(a^n)$ divides $\sigma(b^n)$ for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$. Prove that each prime factor of $\tau(a)$ divides $\tau(b)$.

The incircle $\omega$ of a triangle $ABC$ is tangent to the sides $CB$ and $CA$ at $D$ and $E$, respectively. Point $X$ is the reflection of $D$ in $B$. Suppose that the line $DE$ is tangent to the $A$-excircle at $Z$. Let the circumcircle of triangle $XZE$ meet $\omega$ for the second time at $K$. Prove that the intersection of $BK$ and $AZ$ lies on $\omega$.

A cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with circumcenter $O$ is given, and $P$ is the intersection of the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of the sides $AD$ and $BC$, respectively, and let $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, $\omega_3$ be the circumcircles of triangles $ADP$, $BCP$ and $OMN$, respectively. The intersection point of $\omega_1$ and $\omega_3$ which is not on the arc $APD$ of $\omega_1$ is $E$, and the intersection point of $\omega_2$ and $\omega_3$ which is not on the arc $BPC$ of $\omega_2$ is $F$. Prove that $OF=OE$.
Find all $C\in \mathbb{R}$ such that every sequence of integers $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ which is bounded from below and satisfies $$0\leq a_{n-1}+Ca_n+a_{n+1}<1$$ for all $n\geq 2$ is periodic.

Let $m,n$ and $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_m$ be arbitrary positive integers. Ali and Mohammad play the following game. At each step, Ali chooses $b_1,b_2,\dots,b_m \in \mathbb{N}$, and then Mohammad chooses a positive integer $s$ and obtains the new sequence $c_i=a_i+b_{i+s}$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, where $$b_{m+1}=b_1,\ b_{m+2}=b_2, \ \dots,\ b_{m+s}=b_s.$$ The goal of Ali is to make all the numbers divisible by $n$ in a finite number of steps. Find all positive integers $m$ and $n$ such that Ali has a winning strategy, no matter what the initial values $a_1, a_2,\dots,a_m$ are.

Let $n$ be a positive integer. Consider a regular polygon with $2n$ sides such that one of its longest diagonals is parallel to the $x$-axis. Find the smallest integer $d$ such that there is a polynomial $P$ of degree $d$ whose graph intersects all sides of the polygon at points other than vertices.

In a triangle $ABC$ with $AB<AC$, $I$ is the incenter and $E$ is the point where the $A$-excircle touches $BC$. Point $F$ lies on the external bisector of $\angle BAC$ such that $E$ and $F$ lie on the same side of the line $AI$ and $\angle AIF=\angle AEB$. Point $Q$ lies on $BC$ such that $\angle AIQ=90^\circ$. The circle $\omega_b$ is tangent to $FQ$ and to $AB$ at $B$, the circle $\omega_c$ is tangent to $FQ$ and to $AC$ at $C$, and both circles pass through the interior of triangle $ABC$. If $M$ is the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$, prove that $M$ lies on the radical axis of $\omega_b$ and $\omega_c$.

Consider $n\geq 6$ points $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ in the plane, no three of them collinear. A graph with vertices $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$ is called a road network if it is connected, each edge is a line segment, and no two edges intersect at points other than the vertices. Prove that there are three road networks $G_1,G_2,G_3$ such that no two of them have a common edge.

An infinite set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is called good if for all pairwise distinct integers $a,b,c\in S$, all positive divisors of $\frac{a^c-b^c}{a-b}$ are in $S$. Prove that for every positive integer $n>1$ there exists a good set $S$ with $n \notin S$.

Consider a table with $n$ rows and $2n$ columns. We put blocks in some of the cells. Then we put a robot on a cell, and it starts moving in one of the directions right, left, down or up. It can change direction only when it reaches a block or the border. Find the smallest number $m$ such that we can put $m$ blocks on the table and choose a starting cell for the robot so that it can visit all the unblocked cells. (The robot cannot enter blocked cells.)

Let $G$ be a simple graph with $11$ vertices $v_1 , v_2 , \ldots , v_{11}$ such that the degree of $v_1$ is $2$ and the degrees of the other vertices are $3$. Suppose that for any set $A$ of vertices with $|A| \le 4$, the number of vertices which are adjacent to at least one vertex of $A$ and do not belong to $A$ is at least $|A|$. Find the maximum possible diameter of $G$. (The distance between two vertices is the number of edges of a shortest path between them, and the diameter of a graph is the largest distance between two of its vertices.)

In a right triangle $ABC$ with $\angle A=90^\circ$ we have $AC=2AB$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the side $BC$ and $I$ the incenter of triangle $ABC$. The line through $M$ perpendicular to $BI$ meets the lines $BI$ and $AC$ at $H$ and $K$, respectively. The ray $IK$ meets the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at $F$, and $S$ is the second intersection point of the line $FH$ with the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Prove that $SM$ is tangent to the incircle of triangle $ABC$.
Prove that for all real numbers $x,y,z$ $$(x+y+z)^2 + \frac{(x+y)(y+z)}{1+|x-z|}+\frac{(y+z)(z+x)}{1+|y-x|}+\frac{(z+x)(x+y)}{1+|z-y|} \ge xy+yz+zx.$$
Find all functions $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all real numbers $x,y$ $$f(yf(x)+f(x)f(y))=xf(y)+f(xy).$$

Two natural numbers $x,y \le 100!$ with undetermined values are given. Prove that there exist natural numbers $m,n$ such that the values of $x,y$ are uniquely determined by the value of $\varphi(d(my))+d(\varphi(nx))$. (For each natural number $n$, $d(n)$ is the number of its positive divisors and $\varphi(n)$ is the number of positive integers less than $n$ which are relatively prime to $n$.)

Let $A_1A_2\ldots A_{99}$ be a regular $99$-gon and let $A_{100}$ be its center. Find the smallest natural number $n$ such that Parsa can color all segments $A_iA_j$ ($1 \le i < j \le 100$) with $n$ colors in such a way that no two segments of the same color intersect or share a vertex.

Let $ABC$ and $C'B'A$ be two congruent triangles (with the vertices in this order and with the same orientation). Let $M$ be the midpoint of the segment $AB$, and suppose that the extension of $CB'$ beyond $B'$ passes through $M$. If $F$ is a point on the smaller arc $MC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $BMC$ such that $\angle FB'A=90^\circ$, and $\angle C'CB' \neq 90^\circ$, prove that $\angle B'C'C=\angle CAF$.

Find all functions $f : \mathbb{Q}[x] \to \mathbb{Q}[x]$ such that the following two conditions hold:

• $f(P+Q)=f(P)+f(Q)$ for all $P,Q \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$;

• for all $P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, $\gcd(P , f(P))=1$ if and only if $P$ is square-free.

A polynomial with rational coefficients is square-free if it is not divisible by the square of a non-constant polynomial with rational coefficients.
Prove that for any natural numbers $a,b,c$ with $b>a>1$ and $\gcd(c,ab)=1$ there exists a natural number $n$ such that $$c \mid \binom{b^n}{a^n}.$$

Let $(a_n)$ be a sequence of natural numbers such that every prime number greater than $1402$ divides some term of the sequence. Prove that the set of prime divisors of the terms of the sequence $(b_n)$, where $b_n=a_1a_2\cdots a_n-1$, is infinite.

Let $n<k$ be two natural numbers, and suppose that Sepehr has $n$ chemical elements, $2k$ grams of each, divided arbitrarily among $2k$ cups. Find the smallest number $b$ such that it is always possible for Sepehr to choose $b$ cups containing in total at least $2$ grams of each element.

In a triangle $ABC$ with obtuse angle $\angle A$, let $E,F$ be the feet of the altitudes from $B,C$ on the lines $AC,AB$, respectively. The tangents to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ at $B$ and $C$ meet the line $EF$ at $K$ and $L$, respectively, and $\angle CLB=135^\circ$. Point $R$ lies on the segment $BK$ such that $KR=KL$, and $S$ is a point on the line $BK$ such that $K$ is between $B$ and $S$ and $\angle BLS=135^\circ$. Prove that the circle with diameter $RS$ is tangent to the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$.
